sections.h2: Which Clark County offices set values and send tax bills?
sections.html:
Springfield's A.B. Graham Building, 31 North Limestone Street, houses both offices that touch your tax bill. The auditor (937-521-1860) decides what each parcel is worth. The treasurer (937-521-1832) prints, mails and collects the bills.

On its own page the treasurer's office lists annual collections of $135 million in real estate tax and $275,000 in manufactured home tax. Each bill stacks levies from several local taxing bodies.

For the levy breakdown on your district, ask the treasurer for the yearly rate sheet. The property tax page has a link to it, and the counter hands out paper copies.

The treasurer's main page links to online payment. Written notices, such as a change of mailing address, go to the treasurer at P.O. Box 1305, Springfield, OH 45501-1305.

sections.h2: How often does Clark County reappraise homes?
sections.html:
Clark County's auditor follows a six year reappraisal cycle with a sales-based triennial update halfway through. The auditor's triennial update FAQ separates the two: a reappraisal includes an inspection of each property, and an update looks only at sales. Its 2022 round drew on 2019, 2020 and 2021 sales and priced homes as they stood on January 1, 2022.

The FAQ describes a mass appraisal done by a hired contractor across more than 50,000 residential parcels. It lists location, lot size, age, style, square footage, construction quality, foundation, outbuildings and condition as the factors that feed a value. It also explains the arithmetic behind a bill: appraised value, then 35 percent of it, then the voted levies, yields the gross tax. Most rates are adjusted yearly so each levy raises what it raised the year before.

sections.h2: What are the Clark County payment dates and late charges?
sections.html:
A year of tax comes in two installments. The treasurer's page for the 2025 tax year names February 27, 2026 for the first installment and August 7, 2026 for the second, both now in the past. Later cycles carry their own dates, so rely on the bill itself. Mailing happens 20 to 25 days ahead of each deadline, and the office stresses that never receiving a bill does not cancel the tax or the penalties.

Penalty and interest dates printed on the Clark County Treasurer's property tax page for the 2026 cycle

Mailing a check late in the window carries a trap. Section 323.12 accepts a Postal Service postmark dated by the final day, and rejects a postage meter stamp from a private machine.

sections.h2: Can you spread Clark County property tax into monthly payments?
sections.html:
The treasurer's escrow program converts each half-year bill into equal monthly prepayments. Participants sign an agreement and get coupons showing an estimated amount, though any amount is accepted on any day. Cash, check, money order and ACH debit all work, and the page says the program costs nothing to use.

  • Mail the Escrow Program Form to P.O. Box 1305, Springfield, OH 45501-1305, or email it to treasurer@clarkcountyohio.gov.
  • Whatever your prepayments leave unpaid is due on the regular deadline, or the late penalty applies.
  • Report a new mailing address in writing, since a bill sent to an old address still counts as issued.

Anyone listing a house should ask the treasurer how a prepaid balance is handled at closing.

sections.h2: How can an owner contest a Clark County valuation?
sections.html:
The complaint form goes to the county auditor, and section 5715.19 sets the cutoff: March 31 of the year after the tax year, or the day first-half collection closes if that falls later. Postal postmarks count as the filing date for mailed forms. Owners, their spouses and certain retained professionals can sign.

  • The auditor forwards each complaint to the Clark County Board of Revision, which has 180 days after the filing deadline to hear and decide it.
  • The auditor's FAQ puts the burden on the owner and names a recent arm's length sale, of your home or a similar one, as the strongest proof.
  • During the wait you may tender tax based on the value you claimed, and the treasurer must accept it.
  • One complaint per interim period is the limit unless something changed afterward, such as a sale, a casualty loss or a major addition.

The FAQ recommends starting with the auditor's informal review. Section 5715.19(G) also requires a complainant to give the Board of Revision all evidence in their possession. Anything held back may be barred if the case moves on to the Board of Tax Appeals or the common pleas court, unless good cause is shown.

sections.h2: Which relief programs cut a Clark County tax bill?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption leads the list. The state's tax department FAQ describes a credit for owners aged 65 or more, owners who are permanently and totally disabled, and some surviving spouses. In tax year 2026 it equals the tax charged on $29,700 of value, with a $41,000 income ceiling. Disabled veterans see $59,400 and face no income test.

  • Form DTE 105A (or DTE 105I for veterans) goes to the Clark County Auditor, due December 31 of the credit year.
  • Applicants turn 65 by the end of that year and must have owned and lived in the house since January 1.
  • A denial can be taken to the Board of Revision on DTE 106B inside 60 days.

House Bill 96, signed in June 2025, lets county commissioners add a matching local option. The auditor can say whether Clark County adopted one.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when a Clark County house sells?
sections.html:
A balance stays with the parcel, and the buyer's title search will surface it. Call 937-521-1832 for a payoff figure, hand it to whoever runs the closing, and have it settled out of the proceeds. The penalty and interest steps in the table above continue until the day of payment.

The deed paperwork adds one more tax question. Section 319.202 has the buyer record what the seller says about whether the current or previous year's taxes will be reduced under the homestead or owner-occupancy rules. Know your own answer before closing day, because a yes means a sworn estimate of the reduction travels with the deed.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Clark County homeowners?
sections.html:
West central Ohio's Clark County spans 403 square miles around the seat, Springfield. Wikipedia names two cities, Springfield and New Carlisle, and puts the rural share of 2020 residents at 25.4 percent. From Census QuickFacts:

  • Households (2020 to 2024): 55,975, averaging 2.37 people.
  • Owner-occupied home value at the median: $169,900. Monthly owner costs run $1,262 with a mortgage and $523 without.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 2,196, with 42,831 jobs.
  • Household income at the median: $63,132. Poverty rate: 14.1 percent.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Clark County Treasurer?
faqs.a: Call 937-521-1832, the number the property tax page prints for bill questions. The office is in the Graham Building on North Limestone Street.

faqs.q: What was the last payment date for 2025 Clark County real estate tax?
faqs.a: August 7, 2026, for the second half. February 27, 2026 was the first-half date. A 5 percent penalty and then a 10 percent penalty followed each one.

faqs.q: Who receives a Clark County valuation complaint?
faqs.a: The Clark County Auditor receives it and passes it to the Board of Revision. March 31 of the next year is the cutoff, unless first-half collection closes later.

faqs.q: Is there a way to pay Clark County tax monthly?
faqs.a: Yes, through the treasurer's escrow program, which charges nothing. Send the Escrow Program Form to P.O. Box 1305, Springfield.

faqs.q: How is a Clark County bill calculated from market value?
faqs.a: Per the auditor's FAQ, 35 percent of the appraised value is multiplied by the voted levies to reach the gross tax. Credits come off after that.
